Definition: something stationary, i.e. a prefect, a military post, a statue
BiblicalUsage: A fixed thing is whatever is set up to stand: Lot's wife becomes a pillar of salt, the Philistines hold a garrison on the hill of God, David sets garrisons in Syria, and Geber son of Uri is the one officer in the land of Gilead. Pillar, garrison, and officer are all things planted in place.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that what is set up stays: a pillar of salt stands as a warning, and a garrison stands as a claim — God plants both, and neither moves. Lot's wife stands as salt, and David's garrisons stand as a claim — both of them are fixed, and neither can be moved.
